blocks.text: Matthew turns from Jesus’ completed teaching to the events that lead to his arrest. The chapter places the final meal, Jesus’ distressed prayer at Gethsemane, the disciples’ failure to watch and later flight, and the actions of several parties in the arrest and hearing side by side. Jesus identifies the bread with his body and the cup with his covenant blood, poured out for many for forgiveness; he also speaks of the coming kingdom. The narrative presents his prayer as a real struggle over “the cup,” yet one marked by submission to the Father’s will. It also distinguishes the agency of the various actors in the passion story while recognizing crucifixion as Roman state execution.

In verse 31, Jesus quotes the image of a struck shepherd and scattered sheep. The New Testament explicitly receives Zechariah’s images of a humble king, a struck shepherd, and a pierced figure, while also reusing other imagery from that book. Here the shepherd-and-sheep image helps frame the disciples’ promised scattering as part of the chapter’s scriptural language, immediately before their actual flight at Jesus’ arrest.
